descriptionChirho: Basic act of gathering or picking up items from the ground, such as manna or fallen grain, in the simple Qal stem.
Intensive gathering or gleaning, often in the specific context of gleaning leftover grain in harvested fields (as in Ruth), but also picking up sticks or other items thoroughly.
Passive of the intensive stem, indicating being gathered or picked up by another agent.
Reflexive-reciprocal sense of people gathering themselves together or assembling as a group.
